message.content:
**Killing Visual Studio Code (code.exe) from the Command Prompt**

On Windows you can terminate an application by its image name (`/IM`) or by its process ID (`/PID`).  
For VS Code the executable is called **code.exe**.

---

### 1️⃣ Kill *all* running instances of VS Code

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

* `/IM code.exe` – target the executable named `code.exe`.
* `/F`          – force termination (equivalent to “End Process” in Task Manager).

This will close every instance of VS Code that is currently running.

---

### 2️⃣ Kill a specific instance by PID

If you only want to close one particular window:

1. Find the PID first:

   ```cmd
   tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
   ```

   This lists all `code.exe` processes and their PIDs.

2. Terminate the chosen PID:

   ```cmd
   taskkill /PID <PID_NUMBER> /F
   ```

   Replace `<PID_NUMBER>` with the actual number shown in the list.

---

### 3️⃣ Optional: Wait for graceful shutdown before forcing

VS Code usually shuts down cleanly when you close it normally. If you want to give it a chance to finish tasks before forcing:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /T
```

* `/T` – terminates the specified process and any child processes started by it.  
  (No `/F`, so it will try a normal graceful exit first.)

---

### 4️⃣ Running from PowerShell

In PowerShell you can also use the same `taskkill` command, but you can pipe the output to `Out-Host` for readability:

```powershell
taskkill /IM code.exe /F | Out-Host
```

Or use native PowerShell cmdlets:

```powershell
Get-Process code | Stop-Process -Force
```

---

### 5️⃣ Common pitfalls & tips

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| “Access denied” error | Run CMD or PowerShell **as Administrator**. |
| No matching process found | Make sure VS Code is actually running; check the exact image name (`code.exe`). |
| You see many `code.exe` entries | Each VS Code window may spawn a separate renderer process; `/IM` kills all of them at once. |

---

#### TL;DR

```cmd
:: Close every VS Code window immediately
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

That’s all you need to stop VS Code from the command line!
